approach: Three changes that meet in the throughput review. (1) athena-data: add a small `WasteFigures` struct (attempts per landing, wasted USD, first-attempt share) and a defaulted optional `waste` field on `ThroughputReview`, plus a `Wasted` trigger. Old records still parse. (2) status.rs: compute the three measures from job records over the newest 20 landings and the 20 before them (`waste_windows`), plus the noise between recent windows. Store them on `Throughput` and print them in `Throughput::text()`. `athena status` and `status --snapshot` already print `text()` (display.rs:1114 and :1203), so display.rs and snapshot.rs need no edit. (3) hestia.rs: `throughput_due` gains the current figures and fires `Wasted` when attempts per landing or wasted spend rose more than 20% (WORSEN_RATIO), or the first-attempt share fell more than 20%, against the previous review's stored figures, once a job has landed since. `throughput_review` no longer skips the model because a design request is open: it notes the open request in the record and tells the model about it. A pure gate (`request_gate`) decides whether to ask the model and queue a design request: only when the median or any of the three measures worsened by more than the noise between recent windows, or on the first review. The note says "within noise", "no measure worsened", or that the noise could not be estimated. The slowdown comparison and its 25% rule are unchanged. No parser, stem list or reading rule changes, so refusal_corpus is not touched.

decisions.choice: Attempt = a request job that did work (has invocations) or a landed job. Landing = a landed request job. First-attempt landing = a landed job whose request is not 'try again on <job>' pointing at an earlier job that did work (reading::retried_job, reading.rs:1522, the same link planning_cost uses at status.rs:448). Wasted spend = JobRecords::spent_usd (store.rs:169) summed over attempts that did not land, using the same 'did not land' predicate as unlanded_jobs (status.rs:1016-1018), moved into a shared helper.
decisions.reason: Everything comes from job and invocation records, so no new record type is needed. spent_usd also covers jobs with no outcome totals (a job stopped in planning). The retry link is already the codebase's definition of 'another attempt at the same change'.

rejected.why: Jobs stopped before an outcome carry no totals, and spent_usd is already the sum the rest of status uses.

rejected.option: Count attempts as invocations or producer runs
rejected.why: A job's planner, critic and verifier runs are not attempts to land a change; the request's '58% of attempts did not land' is about jobs.

decisions.choice: Windows: rank all landed request jobs by landing end (the order landed_jobs_among_first uses, status.rs:963). The newest window is the newest 20 landings plus every unlanded attempt that ended at or after the 20th-newest landing. The previous window is landings 21-40 plus unlanded attempts that ended between the two cut times. The previous window is reported only when it holds 20 landings. `waste_windows(records, window)` takes the size as a parameter so tests can use small windows; production passes THROUGHPUT_WINDOW.
decisions.reason: Matches 'newest 20 landings and the 20 before' without a second time axis, and a thin previous window cannot trigger a review.

rejected.why: Landings per day vary a lot, so the window would not be 20 changes.

rejected.option: Count only the measured landed jobs of landed_jobs()
rejected.why: It drops landed jobs that ran no model, which are still landings and still attempts.

decisions.choice: The trigger compares the current figures with the figures stored on the previous review (new `waste: Option<WasteFigures>` on ThroughputReview), exactly as the median trigger compares with window_median_minutes. A previous review with no stored figures gives no waste trigger. Rise tests: attempts per landing > previous x WORSEN_RATIO; wasted USD > previous x WORSEN_RATIO (when previous is 0, any current at or above 0.01 USD); first-attempt share < previous x (2 - WORSEN_RATIO). All need a landing since the previous review.
decisions.reason: A persistent high level then triggers once, not on every landing. It reuses the stored-baseline pattern, and a defaulted optional field keeps old records valid.

rejected.option: Trigger on newest 20 vs the 20 before, recomputed from records
rejected.why: A level that stays high would fire on every new landing, since the window shifts by one each time.

rejected.option: New ThroughputTrigger variant for each measure
rejected.why: One `Wasted` variant is enough. The note names which measures rose, and a record with several variants would need more validation.

decisions.choice: Noise for a measure = the largest absolute difference between adjacent non-overlapping 20-landing windows among the windows older than the newest, from up to 4 windows (so 3 windows, 60 landings, give 2 differences). Fewer than 3 full windows gives None, treated as 0 in the gate and stated in the note. The median's noise uses the same cut over measured landed jobs. Computed in Throughput::compute and stored in a `noise` field.
decisions.reason: This is the 'noise between recent windows' of the accepted reading. It excludes the newest pair, so the change being judged is not part of its own noise. Stating 'not estimated' is honest when history is short.

rejected.option: Standard error of the difference inside the two windows
rejected.why: A principled alternative, but it is not 'noise between recent windows' as accepted, and it needs per-job series for spend and share.
It is just the 20% trigger again and does not adapt to how noisy a repository is.

decisions.choice: An open design request no longer stops the model. The review notes it ('throughput design request <id> is still open; this review ran anyway'), the THROUGHPUT.md given to the model names it so the model does not propose the same change, and a new design request is queued only if the gate says the change is beyond noise. The gate also decides whether the model is asked at all.
decisions.reason: This is what 'does not skip a run' and 'notes the open request instead' need. A review that the gate rejects asks no model, so it costs nothing.

rejected.option: Keep today's behaviour (record a note, skip the model) and only reword
rejected.why: That is what the request calls doing nothing; today's code already writes a record and skips the model (hestia.rs:1728-1733).

rejected.option: Ask the model but never queue while a request is open
rejected.why: The model's proposal would be recorded and acted on by nobody.

decisions.choice: display.rs and snapshot.rs are left unchanged.
decisions.reason: Both only print Throughput::text(); the new lines come from text(), and the status_snapshot test already asserts the printed text contains text(). The test is extended to check the three labels.

rejected.option: Add separate display code for the three measures
rejected.why: It would duplicate text() and could drift from what the review is given.

risks.risk: The gate makes cadence reviews that see no worsening ask no model and queue nothing, which is a behaviour change beyond the trigger wording.
risks.mitigation: That is what 'only queue a request when the change is larger than the noise' asks for. The note says why, and the first review (no previous) still always asks. The changelog and hestia.md state it.

risks.risk: With fewer than 60 landings the noise is not estimable, so any worsening queues a request.
risks.mitigation: The note says the noise was not estimated and how many landings it needs. This is not worse than today, where every review asked.

risks.risk: Two design requests can be open at once.
risks.mitigation: A second is queued only when the change is beyond noise. THROUGHPUT.md lists the open request so the model proposes a different change, and the review note cites it.

risks.risk: Existing hestia tests assert the model is not called while a request is open (4628, 4724, 4790).
risks.mitigation: Step 6 lists and rewrites those assertions. The slowdown assertions stay the same, so the unchanged 25% rule is still covered.

risks.risk: Window and retry reconstruction can drift: a landing record written later moves the landing end, and a 'try again on' link may point at a job that is missing.
risks.mitigation: A missing or unrun predecessor counts as no predecessor (the landing counts as first-attempt), and the doc says the figures are a reconstruction, as previous_stage_medians does.

risks.risk: A new record field makes a newer record unreadable by an older Athena because of deny_unknown_fields.
risks.mitigation: skip_serializing_if keeps the field out of records until the new code writes it. Only forward reading by old binaries is affected, which is already true of every new field in this crate.

demonstrations.method: A new status.rs test builds sample records: 20 landed jobs and 20 failed jobs, via the existing test helper `timed_job` and `loaded`. 10 of the landed jobs are plain requests. The other 10 have the request text `try again on <id>` naming one of 10 of the failed jobs, which did work. The remaining 10 failed jobs are never retried. It sets a 0.50 USD cost on each failed job's invocation. It calls Throughput::compute(&records) and `waste_windows(&records, THROUGHPUT_WINDOW)`.
demonstrations.observes: Attempts per landing is exactly 2.0, the first-attempt share is exactly 0.5, wasted spend is 10.00 USD, and 20 of 40 attempts did not land. A second assertion on a records set with no failures gives 1.0, 1.0 and 0.0.
demonstrations.fails_without: With no `waste_windows` or attempt counting, the test does not compile. With a wrong definition (counting only landed jobs as attempts) attempts per landing would be 1.0, not 2.0.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points `status::waste_windows` and `Throughput::compute`. The fixture is in-memory `Records` built by `timed_job` (pub(crate), status.rs:3261) and `loaded` (status.rs:3343); both exist. A helper that edits request text and invocation cost on the loaded records is added in the test (plan step 7). No double sits in front of the logic under test.

demonstrations.method: A new hestia.rs test calls the pure `throughput_due(landed, median, waste, latest)` with `earlier_review(10, 10.0)` carrying stored figures (attempts 1.5, wasted 2.00 USD, share 0.8). Case A: 15 landed, the same median 10.0, wasted 2.50 USD, the other two figures equal. Case B: wasted 2.50 USD but no landing since the review (10 landed), and wasted exactly 2.40 USD (exactly 20%) with 15 landed. Case C: all three figures equal. Case D: attempts per landing up 25%, then the share down 25%. Case E: a previous review with `waste: None`.
demonstrations.observes: Case A returns Some(Wasted) and Case C returns None, with the median the same in both. Case B returns None for both inputs: no landing since, and exactly 20% is not more than 20%. Case D returns Some(Wasted) each time, and Case E returns None. The existing median cases return Cadence and Worsened exactly as before.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the waste argument and the Wasted branch, Case A returns None, because the median is unchanged.

demonstrations.method: Two tests. (a) Pure: `request_gate(previous, current, noise)` with a rise of 0.1 in attempts per landing against a noise of 0.3 returns queue=false and a note containing 'within noise'. A rise of 0.5 against the same noise returns queue=true and a note naming the measure, the rise and the noise. No noise (None) with any rise queues and says the noise was not estimated. No worsening says 'no measure worsened'. (b) Review level: a records set with three or four 20-landing windows (built with `seed_landed` plus unlanded jobs) whose older windows differ by about 0.3 in attempts per landing. The previous review's stored figure differs from the newest window by 0.1 (then by 0.6), and the fake `throughput_model` is injected.
demonstrations.observes: For the 0.1 change the model log is empty, no design request is queued, and the review note contains 'within noise'. For the 0.6 change the model is called once and one design request is queued.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the gate, the within-noise case still asks the model and queues a request, so the empty model log and the 'within noise' note fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production `hestia::request_gate` (new, pure) and `Athena::throughput_review`. The fixtures are in-memory values for (a) and the existing seed helpers plus fake driver for (b). Step 4 adds `request_gate`. The noise comes from the real `Throughput::compute`, not from a double.
